children.value: Offing reads code it did not write, loads data it did not build at the same time as the code, and gives answers to tools that can edit and install. This page records what v1 trusts, the threats each surface faces, what mitigates them, and what remains.

A repository supplies a status file or a modified baseline that hides its own findings from a reader or an agent.
Findings always name the rule, the file, and the exact line;
is described as a snapshot; a baseline's suppressions are counted and reported; neither can change a rule.
A committed status file can be stale or forged for a human reader, and a pull request can edit the CI baseline. Reviewers must review baseline changes and re-scan.
Malformed, duplicate, or contradictory input makes a parser miss a declaration, crash the scan, or report a wrong location.
Strict parsers; malformed input yields no declaration instead of a guess; unreadable directories are skipped; scans are deterministic.
Detection is declaration-based. A repository can declare one runtime and use another, and an unsupported syntax can hide a usage until a detector learns it.
There is no record of what a scan saw.
Not a logging product; CI keeps the JSON report, and an opt-in local usage log records
A local scan leaves no audit trail by default.
Findings embed file paths and source excerpts that appear in logs, pull request comments, or an agent's context.
Reads stay local; the Action posts a comment only when asked; no Offing service receives results.
Whatever reads the output, including a hosted agent, receives the excerpts and applies its own policy.
A huge file, deeply nested JSON, a symlink cycle, or a pathological source file stalls the scan.
Per-file read caps of about 1 MB, JSON nesting capped at 64, symlinks not followed, unreadable paths skipped, bounded alias and depth budgets in source parsers.
A very large tree still costs time and memory; there is no global wall-clock budget, and CI jobs have their own timeouts.
Repository content achieves execution, or text in a file instructs the agent that reads the findings.

Prompt injection is not preventable by the scanner: a comment, a file name, or a manifest string can try to steer the host. The host's permission model is the boundary.

Lifecycle rules travel as one JSON bundle. The release workflow signs it with Sigstore keyless signing; Offing verifies it offline before use.
A forged bundle claims to carry Offing's rules.
The signature must verify against the exact bytes; the signer must be the release workflow at a
; chain, validity, and transparency-log inclusion are checked against a trusted root shipped in the package.
The trusted root ages. If Sigstore rotates keys and the installed release is too old, new bundles stop verifying and Offing falls back to bundled data.
A file in a valid bundle is altered, removed, or added.

Every file has a SHA-256 and byte count, the manifest has a content digest, extra and missing files are refused, registry content is validated again, and the format version and minimum Offing version must match.
A compromise of the release workflow or of a maintainer who can push a data tag would sign whatever was built. Rule review before
The signing identity is recorded in the public transparency log and can be checked with
Verification is recorded only in local status output.
Updating data reveals what the user is doing.
requests the public release list, the bundle, and its signature; it sends no repository data and no identifier.
The mirror and the network observe the download, as with any file fetch.
An oversized or hostile download exhausts memory or hangs.
20 MB bundle, 1 MB signature, and 4 MB listing caps; 30-second request timeouts; a mirror can be configured but the same signature check still applies; failure falls back to bundled data.
Repeated failed updates can be retried without limit by the user or a script.
Bundles and registries are declarative JSON, validated before use; no rule field is executed.
A correctly signed but wrong rule affects findings until the next data release. Bundles have no revocation list, and a pinned old bundle stays pinned.
option reads a bundle the user names on the command line. It validates the registry schema but does not verify a signature, because the file is the user's own input, like any other path they pass.

reads the release manifest shipped in the package and hashes every file the manifest lists; a changed, shortened, or missing file fails. When a Sigstore bundle for the manifest is present, it verifies offline against the trusted root bundled with the package. The command never uses the network, so it does not verify the npm registry signature or the npm provenance attestation: those are served by the registry, not shipped in the tarball. The report names
as the commands that check them.

The residual risk is the unsigned case. A manifest with no signature detects an accidental or partial change, but an attacker who can rewrite every file can also rewrite the manifest and its digests. Authenticity rests on npm's registry signature and provenance attestation, which need the network, or on a future release that ships a signed manifest.

A host starts a different server, or an unrelated local process claims to be Offing.
There is no listener, port, account, or credential to impersonate; the host launches the process it configured, and the plugins pin an exact published version.
A host that resolves an unpinned
package trusts the registry and cache it resolves from.
A tool changes the repository while "analyzing" it.
Every tool is read-only, has no output, fix, or overwrite option, advertises
, and runs no command; session findings stay in memory; a test calls every tool and fails if the repository tree changes.
The host still has its own write tools. Offing cannot stop an agent from editing after a scan.
Nobody can tell which packages an agent was warned about.
An opt-in usage log appends package, result, severity, and rule IDs to a local file.
Nothing is recorded by default, and the log can be edited or deleted by anyone who can read the file.
Tool results carry repository paths and excerpts into a hosted model.
No Offing-operated service receives results; the host's policy applies;

Update this page in the same pull request as any change to a trust boundary: a new tool that writes, a new network call, a new file format the scanner parses, a new hook, or a change to signature verification. A threat with no mitigation in the table is a bug or an accepted risk that should name its follow-up issue.
